transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

...I suppose it's about work. I'm a translator. Just some... ongoing issues with the project files. 

It's just that for months now, I keep seeing the same pattern. Certain subcontractors, and... one colleague in particular... they keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. Just enough so it looks like my quality control failed. 

I've brought it up, but IT claims the audit trail is clean. But... well, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. So, that's... that's why I'm here, I guess.
Have you ever heard any voices or sounds when no one was around?
No. No, nothing like that. I don't hear things. It's just... the files. That's all.
Aside from the stress at work, how has your mood been lately—have you been feeling down or depressed?
I... no, not really. I mean, I'm tired, obviously. It's exhausting trying to keep track of what they're doing to the files, but... I'm not depressed. Just... stressed, like you said.
Outside of work, do you ever feel that people in your personal life are trying to deceive or work against you?
No. Not really. I mean... my personal life is fine. It's just the people at work, with the files. That's the only thing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, circumscribed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion involving colleagues altering work files and timestamps to sabotage their performance, persisting for several months. Prominent hallucinations, mood episodes, and broader psychosocial impairment are absent, meeting the criteria for Delusional disorder (F22).
